blockers.summary: The one positive the paper protects in its own headline - 'ATR-inhibitor sensitivity is elevated in FET-rearranged lines and it survives a correction for general chemosensitivity ... that group difference is real' - is imported from its source document with the control stripped off. In the same artifact, after the same line-median correction, PACLITAXEL (a tubulin poison the module itself flags is_atr_inhibitor:false) shows a LARGER effect than either ATR inhibitor, and both PARP inhibitors are 2-4x larger. The source document states the bound in terms the paper does not carry.
blockers.evidence: Manuscript lines 59-62 ('That group difference is real and it is recorded where it was measured') and line 113, where the section-0 table marks 'Is ATR-inhibitor sensitivity elevated in FET-rearranged lines after correcting for general chemosensitivity?' with an unqualified check-mark. research/modalities/fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> atr_inhibitor_sensitivity_gdsc.by_drug.*.welch_line_median_corrected: azd6738 delta -0.4911 (t -5.083), ve-822 -0.4233 (t -2.203), paclitaxel -0.5255 (t -3.076), olaparib -1.0163 (t -5.583), talazoparib -2.0653 (t -5.851). The same artifact's _reading field instructs 'Read the CONTROL drugs first, and quote the LINE-MEDIAN-CORRECTED contrast'. The cited source, research/manuscripts/program/emc-post-degrader-options.md lines 409-415, says it plainly: 'paclitaxel, which has nothing to do with DNA repair, matches AZD6738. So this dataset supports "FET-rearranged lines are drug-sensitive, including but not especially to ATR inhibitors"; it does not isolate ATR, and it must not be written as if it did.' The manuscript names paclitaxel exactly once, at line 562, in the unrelated section-5 correlation table where it lands at rho +0.007 - which leaves a reader believing paclitaxel is a clean null in this programme's ATRi work. The paper's only qualifier on the imported claim is 'it is a group difference, not mechanism-tracking', which is a strictly weaker caveat than the one its source imposes.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Carry the source's bound into the headline and into the section-0 table row: after the correction paclitaxel (-0.525, t -3.08) exceeds ceralasertib (-0.491) and the PARP inhibitors are 2-4x larger, so what the GDSC re-cut supports is 'FET lines are broadly drug-sensitive, not especially to ATR inhibitors'. If the sentence keeps 'that group difference is real' with only the mechanism-tracking qualifier, and the section-0 row keeps its bare check-mark, the defect stands.

blockers.summary: Part D's drug-specificity control - the 'vs non-DDR drugs' column, printed with tick and cross marks for every predictor - is a SIGNED mean over two control drugs whose correlations have opposite signs and magnitudes of 0.13-0.26. It cancels to near zero for essentially every expression predictor, INCLUDING the paper's own plain-proliferation control, which the artifact therefore marks atri_specific:true. The counterexample is a row in the paper's own artifact: a predictor the paper defines as the archetype of non-specific passes the paper's specificity bar. Worse, the extra strike the headline lays on the mechanism's load-bearing predictor - 'is the one predictor that also fails the drug-specificity control' - is an artifact of that cancellation, and reverses on the module's own absolute-value version of the same statistic.
blockers.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity. expr::proliferation_MYC: mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors -0.1711, mean_rho_across_non_DDR_controls -0.0139, per_drug paclitaxel -0.1784 (t -4.804) and bortezomib +0.1507 (t 4.04), mean_abs_rho_across_non_DDR_controls 0.1646, atri_specific TRUE. The same pattern holds for every expression predictor the manuscript marks with a tick: expr::replication_stress (printed at line 542 as '+0.037 tick') has per-drug controls paclitaxel -0.1462 (t -3.915) and bortezomib +0.2196 (t 5.963), i.e. its association with bortezomib (0.2196) is LARGER than its association with the ATR inhibitors (-0.1637); signature::FET_fusion_heldout (printed '+0.062 tick') has paclitaxel -0.1413 and bortezomib +0.2645 (t 7.268), mean_abs 0.2029. The producing module documents the failure mode and then does not act on it: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2896-2901 comment 'A SIGNED mean over controls can be small because the controls are null OR because two large opposite-sign associations cancelled. Only the per-drug values and the mean of |rho| distinguish those, so both are emitted. Reporting only.' - and line 2907-2909 computes atri_specific from the signed mean alone (abs(a) > 0.1 and abs(a) > 1.5*abs(c0)). On the |rho| version, expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair is 0.1589, the SMALLEST of the failing expression predictors and smaller than every predictor the manuscript ticks (replication stress 0.1829, ATR-CHK1 0.1831, stalled fork 0.1722, S-phase 0.1777, checkpoint 0.1654, FET signature 0.2029). The manuscript nonetheless singles it out at line 69 (headline) ('is the one predictor that also fails the drug-specificity control') and again at line 583 ('it is also the one predictor that fails the drug-specificity test'). None of the sign cancellation, the |rho| column, or the proliferation control's passing status appears anywhere in the manuscript; the only disclosure about this column, at line 564-565, is that the mean is over two drugs rather than three.
blockers.what_edit_would_break_it: Either report the per-drug control correlations in the section-5 table alongside the signed mean (paclitaxel and bortezomib separately, as is already done for the two ATR inhibitors), and delete the 'one predictor that also fails the drug-specificity control' strike against ATM at lines 69 and 583; or state explicitly that the column is a signed mean that cancels, that on the |rho| version ATM is the most drug-specific of the failing predictors, and that the paper's own MYC-targets proliferation control passes this bar. Keeping the tick/cross column as-is, with the ATM strike, leaves the defect.

p1s.summary: The Bangerter reference is printed with year 2022; the repository's own bibliographic record and this document's own Europe PMC cache both say 2023. Volume and pages are right.
p1s.evidence: Lines 210-212 (§2.2) and line 926 (Appendix) both print 'Bangerter et al., *Hum Cell* 2022;36:446-455, PMID 36316541, doi:10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x'. research/literature/submission-reference-metadata-2026-08-09.json entry '36316541' records: journal 'Human cell', journal_abbrev 'Hum Cell', year 2023, volume '36', issue '1', pages '446-455', doi '10.1007/s13577-022-00818-x', pmcid PMC9813045. The assessment's own artifact agrees: emc-atr-vulnerability.json#part_a_hemcss_identity.literature.results['"H-EMC-SS"'].rows entry for pmid 36316541 gives year '2023'. p1s.summary: Part D's four 'bars fixed before the numbers' are applied with numeric thresholds the paper never states, in a document whose SS1 explicitly promises 'the cuts themselves, stated so they can be checked'. Three undisclosed rules.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2907-2908: `spec[pname]['atri_specific'] = bool(a is not None and c0 is not None and abs(a) > 0.1 and abs(a) > 1.5 * abs(c0))` - the drug-specificity bar is a 0.1 MAGNITUDE FLOOR plus a 1.5x RATIO, neither stated. Line 2926: `srec['beats_the_proliferation_control'] = bool(abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15)` - a 15% MARGIN, while SS5's table column reads only 'vs proliferation control (rho = -0.171)' with 'beats it' / 'is larger'. Line 2965: `out['tracks_mechanism'] = bool(tests and n_pass >= 2)` - the verdict SENSITIVITY_DOES_NOT_TRACK_MECHANISM turns on a >=2-of-4 threshold the paper never prints, though it prints '1 of 4'. By contrast SS1 lists exactly three cuts (>0.2, `bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1`, < -0.5) and I confirmed all three are correctly cited to emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2309-2322 and depmap_sarcoma_dependency.py line 97, and that git log -S shows none has been edited since introduction (all three introduced in 922366a42, no later commit touches them). Numerically none of the undisclosed rules changes a verdict here (passing predictor 0.2123 clears 1.15 x 0.1711 = 0.1968; the three failing expression predictors fail on a plain comparison too), so this is a disclosure defect, not a result defect.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Printing the three thresholds in SS1 alongside the three already there, and adding the >=2-of-4 rule to SS5's 'four bars' sentence. Removing or softening SS1's promise that the cuts are 'stated so they can be checked' would NOT fix it - the bars are load-bearing for SS5's verdict.

p1s.summary: The ATM row's failure of the 'vs non-DDR drugs' control - a claim repeated in the HEADLINE and in SS5 - is caused by the undisclosed |rho| > 0.1 magnitude floor, not by any correlation with the non-DDR control drugs. On the specificity comparison the paper actually shows, the ATM predictor CLEARS the bar by 2.7x.
p1s.evidence: Artifact `part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity['expr::ATM_signalling_DSB_repair']`: mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors = -0.0903, mean_rho_across_non_DDR_controls = -0.0333, atri_specific = false. Applying line 2908: the ratio clause is 0.0903 > 1.5 x 0.0333 = 0.04995 -> TRUE; the floor clause is 0.0903 > 0.1 -> FALSE. The flag is false only because of the floor. The paper's HEADLINE says the ATM predictor 'is the one predictor that also fails the drug-specificity control' and SS5 repeats 'it is also the one predictor that fails the drug-specificity test', while SS5's table prints the column as 'vs non-DDR drugs | -0.033 X'. The column's marks are not monotone in the printed number - -0.033 gets X while +0.062 (held-out FET signature, rho -0.1379) gets a tick and +0.014 gets a tick - so no reader can reconstruct the rule from what is printed. `expr::control_oxphos` (rho -0.0564) is false for the same floor reason.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Either state the bar in full ('|rho| > 0.1 and |rho| > 1.5x the non-DDR control mean') and say the ATM row fails it on magnitude, or relabel the column so the mark is not attributed to the non-DDR comparison. Merely deleting the -0.033 number would hide the inconsistency rather than resolve it.

p1s.summary: Part B's readability filter and the series-choice rule's primary key are applied but never disclosed; the paper states the choice rule as 'more EMC samples', which is the operative tiebreak here but is not the rule.
p1s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 2106-2113: `MIN_SCORED_CONCEPTS = 3` and `_platform_readable` requires `_status == 'scored'` AND >=3 EMC samples AND >=3 comparator samples AND >=3 scored concepts. Line 2142-2145: `_rank_key` sorts on `(-len(readable_platforms), -n_EMC, -max_scored_concepts_on_one_platform, ser)` - the PRIMARY key is the number of readable platforms, not the EMC count. SS3.4 says only 'Which series carries the verdict is decided by a rule fixed before the numbers, and it picked GSE4303 (more EMC samples)', and its table's 'readable?' column shows ticks and crosses with no threshold given. From the artifact, GSE4303 and GSE24369 each have readable_platforms = 1, so the tie did fall to n_EMC (10 vs 6) and the paper's account of the outcome is correct - but the filter that decided readability (3/3/3), and which moved the tier from NOT_ASSESSABLE to WEAK, is nowhere in the paper. `MIN_GROUP_N = 5` (line 335), applied to Part C's Welch tests at lines 2484/2487/2516, is likewise undisclosed.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: One sentence in SS3.4 giving the readability predicate and the full rank order. Changing the thresholds instead would move the tier and is the thing SS1 exists to forbid.

p1s.summary: The document's own headline artifact still cites only the SUPERSEDED preprint identifier for its source hypothesis - the identical one-of-a-pair defect the Appendix says was found and fixed, unfixed in the OTHER producing module.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> `_hypothesis_source`: 'FET fusion oncoproteins disrupt physiologic DNA repair and create a targetable opportunity for ATR inhibitor therapy - bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578 / PMID 37205599'. `grep -o 41811428 emc-atr-vulnerability.json | wc -l` = 0; `grep -o 37205599` = 1. The source constant is emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 3122 ('10.1101/2023.04.30.538578 / PMID 37205599'), with the same in the module docstring (line 10) and at line 859. The Appendix row for this defect reads 'PMID 37205599 cited alone for route 1's mechanism paper ... the version of record is Gracilla et al., Cancer Research 2026;86:2660-2677, PMID 41811428 - already corrected in the companion document's own reference list but not propagated here until a hardening round', and a second row records the pair-defect ('the prose citation had been corrected to the published record while the producing instrument was still fetching only the preprint'). That fix was made in atr_hrd_sarcoma_series.py (lines 118-119 carry MECHANISM_PMID = 41811428 and MECHANISM_PREPRINT_PMID = 37205599, and the artifact records pmid_of_record 41811428 - verified correct). It was not made in emc_atr_vulnerability.py, which produces parts A-D and the framing, and whose SS7 the paper describes as the place 'every number above' lives.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Adding the version of record to `_hypothesis_source` in emc_atr_vulnerability.py and regenerating (--check currently REPRODUCES, so the regeneration is free). Correcting only the manuscript would reproduce the exact pair-defect the Appendix documents.

p1s.summary: SS8's producer header claims '--check re-derives every statement below offline from the committed inputs cache', but SS8.2's four comparative claims about the PUBLISHED version's wording are carried by no artifact - the cache holds only the preprint. (I verified all four claims independently and every one is TRUE; this is a provenance gap, not a factual error.)
p1s.evidence: atr-hrd-sarcoma-series-inputs.json: `mechanism_pmcid` = 'PMC10187251' (the preprint) and `mechanism_fulltext_xml` is the bioRxiv JATS record (journal-title 'bioRxiv', article-id pmid 37205599, 127 occurrences of 'EWSR1-FLI1', 0 of 'EWSR1::FLI1'). `grep -c 'section heading' atr-hrd-sarcoma-series.json` = 0. The artifact itself says `_version_read`: 'PREPRINT' and the paper honestly says the published sentence count is UNKNOWN - but the sentences 'Throughout, ES becomes Ewing sarcoma and EWSR1-FLI1 becomes EWSR1::FLI1', 'the second quotation appears there as a section heading and a figure caption rather than a running sentence' and 'the last is split across a paragraph by the publisher' are assertions about a document the instrument never fetched. Independent check against PMC13223543 (PubMed/PMC full text of PMID 41811428, DOI 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-25-2166): 130 'Ewing sarcoma', 135 'EWSR1::FLI1', 0 'EWSR1-FLI1'; 'Ewing sarcoma patient tumors do not display the genomic scars of HR deficiency' occurs exactly twice, once as a results section heading and once as the Figure 2 caption title; and the final preprint sentence appears split into three sentences ('We find that Ewing sarcoma tumors are not "BRCA-like" (i.e., isolated loss of HR) but rather harbor partial ATM defects. ... These data may explain the lack of clinical responses to PARP inhibitor monotherapy in patients ...'). All four claims are correct.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Either narrow the SS8 header ('--check re-derives every NUMBER below') or run the --fetch the paper already says is needed, so the published-version text is in the cache. Note the published version IS open in PMC (PMC13223543), so the fetch is a $0 CI step, not a paywall problem.

p1s.summary: The inheritance's largest assumption - that the 3' partner does not matter - is never stated in the manuscript. The whole transfer runs through the retained 5' EWSR1 half; EMC's 3' partner is NR4A3, a C4-zinc-finger nuclear receptor, where the mechanism was measured on an ETS (FLI1) and a bZIP (ATF1) partner. The producing sibling artifact names this limit in words; the paper contains no instance of 'nuclear receptor', 'DNA-binding', 'DBD', '3-prime partner' or 'zinc finger'.
p1s.evidence: grep over research/manuscripts/dependency/emc-atr-vulnerability-assessment.md for 'zinc finger|DNA-binding|DBD|nuclear receptor|3.{0,3} partner' returns zero hits. research/modalities/emc-fet-construct-designs.json -> rgg_dose_calibration_and_predictions['NOT predicted'][3] states it: 'The 3' partner is a nuclear receptor with its own DNA-binding domain and its own nuclear behaviour. The source showed a DBD mutation did not change EWSR1-FLI1's DSB localisation, which is reassuring but was measured on an ETS DBD, not a C4 zinc finger.' The section-0 'what still stands' table (line 81) presents the structural precondition census as untouched by parts C and D without carrying that limit, and section 6.2's six-item 'what this CANNOT conclude' list does not contain it either.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Add the 3'-partner assumption to section 6.2's list, or to the section-0 table row, in the artifact's own terms. Leaving both untouched leaves the paper's central inheritance move with its biggest assumption unnamed.

p1s.summary: The census artifact the section-0 table cites first has not been regenerated for the correction the paper's own appendix records. It still names the MINORITY fusion 'emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3', and its top-level comparative verdict holds_against_every_measured_type:true is computed only on that fusion. Applied to the fusion the paper now says is commonest, that boolean flips.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-fet-idr-census.json -> emc_canonical_EWSR1_NR4A3 = {last_fet_residue_retained: 264, rg_dipeptides_retained: 0, precondition_met: true} - the exon-7 fusion the manuscript (line 81) calls type 2, second-commonest. emc_vs_measured_fusions_comparative has emc_RG_retained_fraction 0.0 in all four rows and holds_against_every_measured_type: true. The commonest EMC fusion, per the manuscript and per research/modalities/emc-fet-construct-designs.json constructs[0], retains EWSR1(1-431) with fraction_of_wildtype_RG_retained 0.267. Against the same four measured comparator rows the census admits - EWSR1::FLI1 e7 at 0.0, EWSR1::ATF1 e8 at 0.233, ATF1 e7 at 0.0, ATF1 e10 at 0.267 - the census's own rule emc_loses_at_least_as_much is FALSE for three of the four, so holds_against_every_measured_type would be false. The census's threshold-free verdict_criterion ('rg_dipeptides_retained == 0') also returns NOT_MET for it, the same verdict it gives the measured EWSR1::ATF1 e8 and e10 types. The manuscript's appendix (line 922) records the label drift and says the correction was propagated into the prose; the artifact at this commit was not regenerated.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Regenerate the census over both EMC types (as emc_fet_construct_designs.py already does) so the artifact the section-0 table cites carries the 8/30 row and a comparative verdict computed on the commonest fusion, or state in the table that the census artifact covers type 2 only.

p1s.summary: The grading's leading predicate cannot register the ATM half of the hypothesis in the direction the hypothesis predicts. Part B's 'elevated' cut is strictly one-sided (mean delta > 0.2, upward) and is applied to a concept list that includes ATM signalling / DSB repair - whose mechanism-predicted direction is DOWN, since the lesion under test is IMPAIRED ATM. A tumour set carrying the ATM-defect shadow as depressed ATM transcripts would be scored identically to a null.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py lines 2308-2322: ddr_up_raw, ddr_up_adj, ctrl_up and prolif_up are all '> 0.2' filters in the up direction only; signature_present = bool(ddr_up_raw); signature_specific_to_DDR = bool(ddr_up_adj) and len(ctrl_up) <= 1. No down-direction predicate exists anywhere in the block. The manuscript states the cut this way at line 144 ('A concept counts as elevated at a mean delta > 0.2 ... with no significance requirement') and then reports the predicate 'EMC tumours show the ATM-defect / replication-stress signature | no' in section 6.1. Part D, by contrast, does register the direction correctly (part_d ... _prediction_directions / expectation: 'MECHANISM PREDICTS rho > 0: lower ATM signalling => more sensitive'), so the asymmetry is between the two parts of the same document. The observed values happen to be flat (GSE4303 ATM +0.113 raw / -0.070 adjusted; GSE24369 -0.004 pooled, -0.001 vs the FET arm), so the conclusion is not reversed - but nothing in the analysis would have told the two cases apart.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State in section 1 or 3.4 that the elevation cut is one-sided and therefore tests the replication-stress/ATR half of the signature only, and that the ATM half is read from the reported deltas being flat rather than from the predicate. Leaving section 6.1's predicate row as a two-sided-sounding 'no' leaves it.

p1s.summary: Part C's group composition is not disclosed, and it contaminates in both directions. The manuscript presents 'FET status from DepMap's own filtered fusion calls, never from disease labels' as a rigour improvement; the artifact shows the 20-line FET group includes osteosarcoma and UPS/MFH lines (not FET-fusion-driven diseases) and the 71-line 'fusion-negative' comparator includes Ewing sarcoma lines.
p1s.evidence: research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_c_coordinated_dependency.fet_lines_subtype_labels = ['Clear Cell Sarcoma', 'Ewing Sarcoma', 'Osteosarcoma', 'Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma/Malignant Fibrous Histiocytoma/High-Grade Spindle Cell Sarcoma']; matched_comparator_subtype_labels includes 'Ewing Sarcoma'. The artifact states the second half of this in _comparator_caveat ('A caller miss puts a FET-positive line in the comparator, which biases the contrast toward the null') and the sibling artifact fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> fet_grouping_by_fusion_call._caveat states the first ('a called EWSR1/FUS/TAF15 fusion is not automatically the ONCOGENIC driver fusion - read this as a wider, noisier grouping than the label one, and use the disagreement between the two as the uncertainty, not either alone'; agreement_with_label_grouping: n_both 18, n_call_only 37, n_label_only 10). Neither caveat appears in manuscript section 4, which says only '20 FET-called sarcoma lines ... against 71 sarcoma-lineage lines with CRISPR data and no FET call'. The saturation finding (99.2-100% of lines below -0.5, delta -0.0065 against SD 0.190) is independently sufficient for the INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND verdict, so this does not change part C's conclusion - it changes what a reader believes the groups were.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Print the two subtype label lists, or at minimum the two caveats already written in the artifacts, in section 4. Leaving 'never from disease labels' standing as an unqualified virtue leaves it.

p1s.summary: The superseded 'PMID 37205599 alone' citation for route 1's mechanism paper still stands in this manuscript's OWN producing script and therefore in its OWN artifact, and in two modality documents the manuscript points readers at - including the preregistration.
p1s.evidence: The Appendix (line ~934) registers 'PMID 37205599 cited alone for route 1's mechanism paper (Menon et al., the bioRxiv preprint)' as superseded, with the version of record Gracilla et al., Cancer Research 2026;86:2660-2677, PMID 41811428. At commit 0448a27a6 the following still cite 37205599 alone, with no mention of 41811428: research/modalities/emc_atr_vulnerability.py line 10 (module docstring) and line 3122; research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json line 5 `_hypothesis_source` = 'FET fusion oncoproteins ... - bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.04.30.538578 / PMID 37205599' (this is THE artifact §7 says every number in the paper comes from); research/modalities/emc-atri-prereg.md line 92 (the preregistration, cited by §0, §6.2 and §6.3); research/modalities/emc-atri-outreach-DRAFT.md lines 39 and 58 (cited by §8.4); research/modalities/emc_fet_idr_census.py lines 20 and 383 and research/modalities/emc-fet-idr-census.json line 3 (the structural-precondition module cited in §0's 'what still stands' table); research/modalities/emc_fet_construct_designs.py lines 21 and 914 and emc-fet-construct-designs.json line 6. `grep -rn 41811428` finds it in the two dependency manuscripts and in program/emc-post-degrader-options.md only - it reaches no modality script, no modality artifact and no prereg. The paper's own §8.2 sets the standard it fails here: 'the attribution above names both identifiers instead of one'.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Add the version-of-record identifier alongside the preprint in emc_atr_vulnerability.py's `_hypothesis_source` string (which regenerates into the artifact), in emc-atri-prereg.md, and in the two census/construct modules. Leaving the artifact's `_hypothesis_source` naming only 37205599 keeps the defect.

p1s.summary: §3.0a prints 'the broad NR4A3 query returns 10,332' - the artifact has said 10,331 since 2026-08-09. The superseded 10,332 comes from artifact commit ce630e2b4, the exact snapshot the Appendix already names as the source of three other stale claims; this is a fourth survivor of it.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §3.0a, the four-archive table row 'EMBL-EBI BioStudies / ArrayExpress ... 37 hits on the disease name (the broad NR4A3 query returns 10,332 and is not usable as a filter)'. Artifact at this commit: emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_b_emc_tumour_signature.dataset_search.biostudies.total_per_query = {'"extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma"': 37, 'NR4A3 sarcoma': 10331}. History: `git log -S'10332' -- research/modalities/emc-atr-vulnerability.json` returns ce630e2b4 (2026-08-05) and 816cbeaac (2026-08-09); `git log -S'10331'` returns 816cbeaac only. Reading the two blobs directly confirms 10332 at ce630e2b4 and 10331 at 816cbeaac and at HEAD. The Appendix's own last-but-one row says 'The snapshot is artifact commit ce630e2b4' and lists n_mapped 20,324, accession_resolution_rate 0.932 and '4,303 -> 4,303 -> 59 linked' as its other survivors - all three of which have been fixed. This one was not. (37 is correct.)
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Print 10,331. Re-introducing 10,332, or quoting any other figure from ce630e2b4, re-breaks it.

p1s.summary: §3.0a says the GEO search returned '25 EMC-titled SAMPLE records', and repeats it as 'the 25 EMC-titled GSMs'. The artifact returned 25 sample records of which 11 are EMC-titled - in every committed version of the artifact, so this is a mis-transcription in a table the section itself calls the deliverable.
p1s.evidence: manuscript §3.0a table row 'NCBI GEO DataSets | 5 ... | 35 UIDs -> 10 series, plus 25 EMC-titled SAMPLE records', and the paragraph below it 'GEO's DataSets summaries for the 25 EMC-titled GSMs came back with an empty series field'. Artifact: part_b_emc_tumour_signature.dataset_search.geo has n_uids = 35 (correct), 10 series (correct), and len(samples) = 25 of which sum(is_emc_titled) = 11. The 11 are GSM600934-GSM600939, GSM715466/715467/715470/715472 and GSM9037837 - and §3.0 itself lists only ten of them by accession. Checked across artifact commits ce630e2b4, 816cbeaac and ad87aa4c7 (HEAD): 25 samples / 11 EMC-titled in all three, so no regenerated value ever supported 25. The section's own framing is 'when the answer is "nothing readable exists", the search record IS the deliverable', which is what makes a 2.3x overstatement of the EMC-titled yield worth fixing.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State '25 SAMPLE records, 11 of them EMC-titled' and fix the second sentence to '25 GSMs'. Any wording that attaches 'EMC-titled' to 25 re-breaks it.

p1s.summary: The one mechanism test the paper reports as PASSING clears its proliferation bar by rho 0.0155 - 0.41x the standard error the paper itself computes - and the bar is an undisclosed 1.15x multiplier applied across two different measurement scales and two different line sets. The paper applies interval reasoning to three other rho comparisons in the same section and not to this one.
p1s.evidence: emc_atr_vulnerability.py derive_part_d: `srec["beats_the_proliferation_control"] = bool(abs(rho) > abs(prolif_rho) * 1.15)`. Artifact emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_d_drug_response_correlation.specificity: dependency::ATR_ATRIP_CHEK1_mean_gene_effect mean_rho_across_ATR_inhibitors = 0.2123; proliferation_control_rho = -0.1711. Bar = 1.15 x 0.1711 = 0.19677; margin = 0.01553. The paper's own SI-grade statement (section 5): "At n ~ 700 the standard error on a single rho is ~ 0.038" (verified: 1/sqrt(697) = 0.0379). The two rho are not measured on the same lines or the same scale: the dependency rho is n=597 (azd6738) / n=565 (ve-822) CRISPR-and-drug lines, the proliferation rho is n=704 / n=711 expression-and-drug lines (artifact correlations block). The module states the scale problem in a comment - "a dependency predictor is on a different scale and sign from an expression predictor ... only meaningful as 'is this bigger than growth rate'" - and section 5's table renders it as a bare tick, "vs proliferation control (rho = -0.171) | checkmark beats it". Neither the 1.15x factor, the margin, the differing n, nor the scale caveat is printed.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Print the bar as it is coded (|rho| > 1.15 x |rho_proliferation| = 0.197), print the margin (0.212 vs 0.197), and extend the section's own interval sentence to this row: at SE ~ 0.04 the passing predictor is not separable from the proliferation control either. Removing or weakening the existing 'no interval is computed anywhere' paragraph would re-break it.

p1s.summary: Part C's 'properly matched fusion-negative sarcoma comparator' shares members with the exposure class: its own subtype list contains Ewing Sarcoma, and the sibling artifact records ten sarcoma lines that are FET by disease label but not by the caller. The paper says the old comparator's limitation 'is now removed'.
p1s.evidence: emc-atr-vulnerability.json -> part_c_coordinated_dependency.matched_comparator_subtype_labels contains 'Ewing Sarcoma' (alongside Chordoma, Leiomyosarcoma, Synovial Sarcoma, ...). The FET group is contaminated in the opposite direction: fet_lines_subtype_labels = ['Clear Cell Sarcoma','Ewing Sarcoma','Osteosarcoma','Undifferentiated Pleomorphic Sarcoma/MFH/High-Grade Spindle Cell Sarcoma'] - osteosarcoma and UPS are not FET-driven diseases. fet-ddr-axis-scan.json -> fet_grouping_by_fusion_call.agreement_with_label_grouping = {'n_label_only': 10, 'n_call_only': 37, 'n_both': 18}, with grouping.FET_rearranged.Ewing.n_with_crispr = 27 and grouping.n_FET_lines_total = 28 by label against 55 by call; that artifact's own _caveat says to 'use the disagreement between the two as the uncertainty, not either alone'. The producing module carries the bias note (_comparator_caveat, 'a caller miss puts a FET-positive line in the comparator'); the manuscript carries neither the note nor the count, and section 4 states 'That limitation is now removed'. Direction: contamination biases toward the null, which is the reported result, so the verdict INSTRUMENT_STILL_BLIND is not overturned - the overclaim is 'removed'.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Replace 'that limitation is now removed' with the two disagreement counts (10 label-only, 37 call-only, 18 both) and name Ewing Sarcoma as present in the comparator, stating that the contamination runs toward the null the section reports. Dropping the counts again would re-break it.

p1s.summary: Part B's 'elevated' cut of 0.2 is read against no reference distribution, and the artifact already contains an empirical one that reaches 1.7x the cut. On the verdict-carrying platform, two COMPARATOR groups that contain no EMC differ by more than any DDR concept does.
p1s.evidence: Recomputed from emc-atr-vulnerability.json per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290_series_matrix.txt.gz'].scores using the same Welch as the module (GIST n=3 vs DFSP n=3, no EMC in either arm): control_oxphos delta +0.334 (t 4.97), proliferation_mitotic -0.089 (t -3.63), ATR_CHK1_activity -0.173 (t -2.29), control_adipogenesis +0.098 (t 2.69). The three DDR concepts the paper counts as clearing the cut are +0.245, +0.311, +0.256. So an arbitrary sarcoma-pair contrast on this platform reaches 0.334, above the 0.2 cut and above every DDR term. This matters for WHICH negative is reported, not whether it is negative: `signature_present = bool(ddr_up_raw)` is what selects GENERIC_ONLY (tier WEAK) over the stronger NO_DDR_SIGNATURE_IN_EMC_TUMOURS verdict (emc_atr_vulnerability.py L2322-2330). The paper states the underpowering honestly - 'Part B's nulls are at n = 10 and n = 6 EMC tumours and no minimum detectable effect was computed' - but never takes the free empirical null sitting in its own scores block.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: Add the comparator-vs-comparator contrast as the empirical null beside the 0.2 cut (GIST vs DFSP: oxphos +0.334, t 4.97) and say that raw elevation of three DDR concepts at +0.245 to +0.311 sits inside it, so the WEAK tier's 'signature_present = yes' predicate is a threshold crossing rather than a measured signal. Deleting the 'no minimum detectable effect was computed' sentence would make it worse.

p1s.summary: An undisclosed design confound in the verdict-carrying contrast: on GPL3290 the EMC and DFSP samples were hybridised against a CRH reference and the GIST samples against UHR (Universal Human Reference), so group and reference channel are partly collinear in a two-colour log-ratio readout. The paper says 'on the same print run', which is true of the array and not of the reference.
p1s.evidence: emc-atr-vulnerability.json per_platform['GSE4303-GPL3290...'].sample_annotations_verbatim: the 10 EMC rows read 'STT3699-Myxoid Chondrosarcoma | CRH-mRNA | ...', the 3 DFSP rows 'STT3126-DFSP | CRH | ...', the 3 GIST rows 'STT2001c-GIST-Total RNA-WT | UHR | ...'. The same block records value_kind = 'two-colour log-ratio vs a reference pool (RELATIVE)'. Per-sample z-scoring against each sample's own background removes scale but not the reference's gene-wise composition. Recomputed with the reference held constant (EMC n=10 vs DFSP n=3, both CRH): ATR-CHK1 +0.158 (t 2.74), S-phase/E2F +0.281 (t 3.81), DNA-damage checkpoint +0.250 (t 3.41), MYC targets +0.376 (t 5.20), oxphos +0.551 (t 8.04), adipogenesis +0.267 (t 6.66). The qualitative reading - DDR concepts move, non-DDR controls move as much or more - is unchanged, so this is a disclosure defect rather than a refutation.
p1s.what_edit_would_break_it: State in section 3.4 that half the six-sample comparator was hybridised against a different reference RNA than the EMC arm, and give the reference-matched EMC-vs-DFSP contrast as the check that the reading survives. Leaving 'on the same print run' as the only design statement re-breaks it.
